name: Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG)

lead: hCG is the hormone made by the placenta that pregnancy tests detect. It mimics luteinizing hormone, so doctors use it to trigger ovulation and to stimulate the testes in some men with hypogonadism.

In looksmaxxing circles it is mainly used by men on testosterone or steroids to keep testes working and fertility intact. Claims for facial growth, height or penis size have not been tested in trials.

paras: hCG binds the luteinizing hormone receptor. In men this stimulates the testes to make testosterone and supports sperm production, which are otherwise suppressed when outside testosterone shuts down the pituitary signal.

It is a prescription injectable in the US; non-prescription hCG weight-loss products are unapproved. Because it raises testosterone and so estradiol, users report needing to monitor hormones. Ovarian hyperstimulation is a known complication in fertility treatment.

lead: Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) is a glycoprotein hormone made by the placenta after implantation, consisting of an alpha subunit shared with other gonadotropins and a hormone-specific beta subunit. It sustains the corpus luteum and progesterone production in early pregnancy and is the basis of pregnancy tests [1][2]. Because it acts on the luteinizing hormone receptor, it is used as a prescription injectable to trigger ovulation in fertility treatment and to stimulate the testes in some men with low testosterone [1][3][4].

In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding communities hCG is discussed as an add-on for men using testosterone or anabolic steroids, to maintain testicular size and fertility while the body's own luteinizing hormone signal is suppressed. Some forum posts also propose it for facial masculinity, penile growth or alongside growth hormone for height, uses for which no trial evidence was found [5][6][7]. Clinical literature supports hCG for inducing puberty and spermatogenesis in men with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, and reviews list it among options for steroid-induced hypogonadism [4][8].

paras: In assisted reproduction, hCG, urinary or recombinant, triggers final oocyte maturation; trials compare the two forms and strategies to reduce ovarian hyperstimulation [9][10][11][12]. In men with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, testosterone alone promotes virilization but not testicular growth or spermatogenesis; a 2024 systematic review of 103 studies with 5,328 patients found that hCG was the most commonly used gonadotropin, in 93 studies [8]. Early-stage research has also tested hormonal stimulation of spermatogenesis in men with non-obstructive azoospermia [13]. hCG is also a tumor marker for gestational trophoblastic disease and germ cell tumors [1][14].

subs.h: Use with testosterone and anabolic steroids
paras: A 2014 review in Fertility and Sterility noted that symptomatic hypogonadism can follow anabolic steroid use, that management may include testosterone replacement, hCG and selective estrogen receptor modulators, and that no studies met the criteria for a formal meta-analysis [4]. A 2025 meta-analysis of randomized trials in functional hypogonadism found that clomiphene or enclomiphene raised testosterone, LH and FSH compared with placebo, and compared the SERMs and combined treatment with hCG [15]. Forum members on looksmax.org and T Nation use hCG to try to prevent testicular atrophy and protect fertility during testosterone use [16][17][18][19].

Randomized and observational studies of hCG address women's fertility treatment [9][10][11] and male hypogonadotropic hypogonadism [8]. A review of steroid-induced hypogonadism, which discusses hCG, found no study of sufficient quality for a meta-analysis [4]. A systematic review and meta-analysis of SERMs for male hypogonadism included comparisons against hCG [15]. A phase 1 trial enrolled 100 men with non-obstructive azoospermia in hormonal stimulation of spermatogenesis [13].

No clinical trial has tested hCG for facial masculinity, penile size or height in people without an endocrine disorder. Grokipedia states that hCG promoted in very-low-calorie diets for weight loss lacks substantiation, with clinical evidence showing no effect beyond calorie restriction [1].

Because hCG stimulates testicular testosterone and estrogen production, forum posters report the need to manage estradiol alongside it; a looksmax.org poster notes that hCG increases testosterone, which is converted to estradiol [5]. In fertility treatment, ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome is a recognised complication, and trials examine ways to prevent it [12][20]. Posters on T Nation describe mixed experiences stopping hCG, including feeling worse after stopping and mood and weight changes after stopping an aromatase inhibitor and hCG [21][22].

In 1927 Selmar Aschheim and Bernhard Zondek developed a biological pregnancy test, the Aschheim-Zondek test, by detecting gonadotropic activity, later attributed to hCG, in the urine of pregnant women [1]. Rabbit-based and then immunological and radioimmunoassay methods followed in the 1930s, 1960 and 1970s [1]. Recombinant gonadotropins, including hCG, were produced after the genes for the subunits were cloned [3].

In the US, hCG is a prescription-only injectable. Non-prescription products such as oral drops, pellets or sprays marketed for weight loss are not FDA-approved and are considered unapproved new drugs [1]. A T Nation user reported that an endocrinologist prescribing testosterone would not also prescribe hCG, so he sourced it himself [18].

On looksmax.org, hCG appears in threads about how long into a first testosterone cycle to start it, whether it is needed for a lower-dose cycle, and whether to run it long term with enclomiphene [16][17][23][24]. Other threads ask about using it with growth hormone for facial growth or height, with DHT gel for penile growth, or as a facial-masculinity tool [5][25][26][27]. Members dispute some of these claims in the threads themselves [5].

lore.intro: hCG is a staple of looksmax.org and T Nation conversation about testosterone and steroid use, usually as a way to keep testes active, and occasionally as a face, height or penis-growth tool [5][16][18][27].
